source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Game of 24 headline
finding: ToT with GPT-4 solves far more Game of 24 than chain of thought, and the gain grows with breadth.
limits: Single task, 3 shallow steps, GPT-4, 100 games, one run. The task was chosen because GPT-4 failed it.
agent_relevance: S6 idea tree can beat plain chains only where early steps are checkable and wrong first steps are common.
quote: while GPT-4 with chain-of-thought prompting only solved 4% of tasks, our method achieved a success rate of 74%

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: equal-budget comparison
finding: Authors' own fair-compute check: best of 100 CoT samples (oracle) reaches 49%, still below ToT. About 60% of CoT samples fail at the very first step.
numbers: Best-of-100 CoT 49% vs ToT b=5 74%. ~60% of CoT chains invalid after step 1 (e.g. 4 + 9).
limits: Best-of-k is scored as an oracle; ToT also uses its own value model, not an oracle. Node-count matching ignores prompt tokens.
agent_relevance: Search pays when the failure sits at the first step; this matches a trigger on early-step checks, not a schedule (G1).

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: cost appendix B.3
finding: ToT costs about as many generated tokens as 100 CoT runs and costs more money; on creative writing about 5x. General range 5-100x CoT tokens.
numbers: Game of 24: ToT 5.5k completion tokens vs CoT-100 6.7k; ToT $0.74/case (74%), CoT best-100 $0.47 (49%), IO best-100 $0.13 (33%). Creative writing ToT ~5x tokens. Whole main experiments ~$106.
limits: GPT-4 2023 prices. Table text was column-garbled in extraction; pairing of cost to row inferred from the success column.
agent_relevance: Budget cap per idea tree is mandatory; the schema must count tokens in code.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Mini Crosswords and ablations
finding: DFS with pruning and backtracking lifts 5x5 crosswords from near zero; removing backtracking or pruning hurts a lot.
numbers: Letter/word/game: IO 38.7/14/0, CoT 40.6/15.6/1, ToT 78/60/20 (4 of 20 games). Oracle best state 82.4/67.5/35 (7/20). No pruning 65.4/41.5/5. No backtracking 54.6/20/5.
limits: Only 20 games. Output heuristic picks the deepest state and misses solved boards; evaluator sometimes prunes correct words.
agent_relevance: Pruning and backtracking carry the gain; sampling alone does not. Keep prune and backtrack operators in S6.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: creative writing and weaker model
finding: Gains shrink or shift with model strength and task type. GPT-3.5 ToT on Game of 24 only 19%. Zero-shot ToT adds little on tasks GPT-4 already solves.
numbers: Game of 24 GPT-3.5: IO 6%, CoT 3%, ToT 19%. Creative writing coherence (1-10) GPT-4: IO 6.19, CoT 6.93, ToT 7.56; GPT-3.5: 4.47, 5.16, 6.62. GSM8K IO 51, CoT 86, ToT 90; StrategyQA 73/82/83 (GPT-4, zero-shot ToT).
limits: Coherence scored by GPT-4 and humans on a self-invented task. Authors state ToT may be unnecessary where GPT-4 already excels.
agent_relevance: Boundary: search adds 4 points over CoT on GSM8K at several times the cost. Do not search on easy items.
quote: Deliberate search such as ToT might not be necessary for many existing tasks that GPT-4 already excels at

source: Long (2023) Large Language Model Guided Tree-of-Thought
finding: Independent ToT variant with a rule-based controller and a checker on Sudoku. ToT beats zero/one/few-shot prompting, but not fully.
numbers: Sudoku, 10 puzzles each size (3x3, 4x4, 5x5). ToT solved 10/10 3x3, 9/10 4x4, 8/10 5x5 (hit the 100-round cap). Authors report ToT 80% (4x4) and 60% (5x5) higher than one/few-shot.
limits: Tiny N=10 per size, no confidence intervals. Controller has no sense whether a partial board can be completed, so search wastes rounds.
agent_relevance: A code controller with a feasibility check is what a tree needs; N=10 evidence is weak.

source: Besta et al. (2023) Graph of Thoughts
finding: GoT (merge and refine nodes) reduces errors on decomposable tasks over ToT and cuts cost, mainly through divide and merge, not deeper search.
numbers: Sorting with GPT-3.5: quality +62% over ToT, +70% over CoT, cost down >31% vs ToT. Median errors down 61% at P=64 and 69% at P=128 vs ToT2; at P=32 only negligible gain over ToT2.
limits: GPT-3.5 only (Llama-2 was worse and too slow). Tasks are sorting, set intersection, keyword counting, merging: decomposable by design. Gain grows with problem size.
agent_relevance: Graph merge helps only when the task splits into parts the code can score. No evidence for open-ended ideation.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: MCTS with the LM as world model and reward gives large gains on Blocksworld planning, with LLaMA-33B.
limits: At 6 steps RAP(20) only just passes GPT-4 CoT (0.42 vs 0.40) and RAP(10) is below it (0.26). Small test sets (30 two-step, 57 four-step cases). Long-horizon still hard.
agent_relevance: Explicit state tracking plus search helps planning-like items; accuracy still falls with depth.

source: Hao et al. (2023) RAP: math and logic
finding: On GSM8k and ProntoQA, RAP beats CoT and self-consistency but the margin on GSM8k is modest.
numbers: GSM8k (LLaMA-33B): RAP(1) 48.6%, RAP(10) 51.6%, one chosen trace 48.8%, aggregation adds ~3 points. ProntoQA: answer 94.2%, proof accuracy 78.8%, +14 proof points over CoT, +4.4 answer points over CoT-SC. Full Blocksworld Llama-2 70B: CoT overall 0.08 (easy) and 0.05 (hard); CoT 0.00 at 12 steps.
limits: GSM8k ablations on first 300 examples. MCTS iterations not matched to sampling in every table.
agent_relevance: Search over reasoning steps gives single-digit gains on arithmetic; large gains only where a state model exists.

source: Zhou et al. (2023/ICML 2024) Language Agent Tree Search (LATS)
finding: LATS (MCTS + reflection + LM value) tops ToT and RAP on HotpotQA, HumanEval, WebShop, Game of 24 with the same LM.
numbers: HotpotQA EM GPT-3.5: base 0.32, CoT 0.34, CoT-SC 0.38, ToT 0.55, RAP 0.60, LATS 0.62. HumanEval pass@1 GPT-3.5: CoT 46.9, ReAct 56.9, ToT 54.4, RAP 63.1, Reflexion 68.1, LATS 83.8; GPT-4: base 80.1, Reflexion 91.0, LATS 92.7. Game of 24 GPT-3.5: CoT 0.08, ToT 0.20, RAP 0.40, LATS 0.44.
limits: Baselines re-run by the authors with their own settings. LATS uses more samples per task (n=5 nodes, k=30-50 trajectories). WebShop LATS score 75.9 vs fine-tuned expert 82.1 (SR 59.6).
agent_relevance: Search with real execution feedback (tests) is the strong case: HumanEval gains rest on a test signal.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) LATS: ablations and limits
finding: Ablation shows the LM value heuristic and the tree both matter; reflection helps less.
numbers: HotpotQA EM, ReAct base, n=5, k=50: no LM heuristic 0.37, DFS instead of MCTS 0.42, no reflection 0.58, full LATS 0.63. ToT(ReAct) 0.39, RAP(ReAct) 0.54.
limits: Authors list higher compute cost and an assumption that the environment can be reverted to earlier states as limits.
agent_relevance: Learned or checked value signal is the active ingredient; drop it and a tree is no better than a chain.

source: Gandhi et al. (2024) Stream of Search
finding: Training on whole search traces (with mistakes and backtracking) beats training on optimal solutions only, on Countdown.
numbers: Held-out accuracy 51.27% SoS vs 25.73% optimal-path model. Dataset 285,501 trajectories, 57.1% correct. After APA/STaR finetuning, solves 36% of previously unsolved problems and ~4% of hard ones; STaR adds ~5-6 points.
limits: Small model trained from scratch on one synthetic task; not a prompted scaffold. Not tested on natural language reasoning.
agent_relevance: Shows search inside the stream can be learned, but our agent is training-free: not directly usable.

source: Chen et al. (2024) When is Tree Search Useful for LLM Planning? It Depends on the Discriminator
finding: Tree search and iterative correction only beat plain re-ranking when the discriminator is at least about 90% accurate; real LLM discriminators are below that.
numbers: Text-to-SQL and math. Tree search at least 10-20x slower than re-ranking with negligible gains. Observation-enhanced discriminators gain up to +30.2 (SQL) and +8.4 (math) points, still barely enough.
limits: Two tasks; LLM discriminators of 2024. Gains depend on oracle-like feedback which rarely exists.
agent_relevance: Strongest argument for G3/G5: the value signal must be code or a held-out check, not model opinion.
quote: advanced planning methods demand discriminators with at least 90% accuracy to achieve significant improvements over re-ranking

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally
finding: Search against a process reward model helps, but its value depends on question difficulty. Compute-optimal allocation beats best-of-N with about 4x less compute.
numbers: MATH. Beam search vs best-of-N: on easy (levels 1-2) beam search degrades as budget grows (PRM exploitation); on levels 3-4 beam search consistently better; at level 5 neither progresses. Compute-optimal strategy ~4x less compute than best-of-N.
limits: PaLM 2-S* with a trained PRM; MATH only. Gain depends on a trained verifier.
agent_relevance: Use search only on hard-but-possible items; on easy items extra search hurts. Needs a difficulty signal (e.g. agreement across attempts).

source: Wu et al. (2024) Inference Scaling Laws (REBASE)
finding: MCTS has a poor compute-accuracy tradeoff; a simple reward-balanced tree search matches or beats weighted voting at equal FLOPs, and small models with search beat big models.
numbers: MATH500/GSM8K: Llemma-7B with REBASE beats Llemma-34B with majority voting at all compute budgets. MCTS often needs dozens of times more generated tokens than sampling and was dropped from main comparisons for poor compute-accuracy.
limits: Needs a trained reward model; math only. Gains are about cost, not new capability.
agent_relevance: Plain sampling plus code selection is a hard baseline; any idea tree must beat it at equal tokens.

source: Katz et al. (2024) Thought of Search
finding: LLM-guided ToT, RAP, LATS are neither sound nor complete and very costly. Having the LLM write the successor and goal-test code solves Game of 24 completely.
numbers: Game of 24: 1362 problems, 1361 solvable; LLM-written successor and goal test plus BFS found all and reported the unsolvable one: 100%, total 1.92-6.83 s, a handful of LLM calls. ToT reported 75%. Same approach 100% on mini crosswords (20 games).
limits: Needs a task that can be formalised in code; heuristic function left to future work.
agent_relevance: Direct fit: code runs the tree (G5), model writes only slot content. Small game rules go to code.

source: Xie et al. (2023) Self-Evaluation Guided Beam Search
finding: Stochastic beam search with step self-evaluation improves few-shot reasoning over Codex baselines.
numbers: GSM8K +6.34, AQuA +9.56, StrategyQA +5.46 points over Codex baselines (StrategyQA 77.2 vs 73.2). Llama-2 results at matched compute.
limits: Self-evaluation is a model judgement, which later work shows is poorly calibrated.
agent_relevance: Step-level pruning helps modestly; keep the judge outside the loop.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1 appendix: unsuccessful attempts
finding: Authors tried MCTS for training and test-time scaling and gave up: token space too large, fine-grained value model too hard to train.
numbers: MCTS with a pre-trained value model improved inference but iterative self-improvement via search was a significant challenge. No benchmark numbers given.
limits: Negative result without numbers; a different use (training) than prompting.
agent_relevance: Even at frontier scale, explicit step trees lost to long single chains; keep the tree small.
quote: while MCTS can improve performance during inference when paired with a pre-trained value model, iteratively boosting model performance through self-search remains a significant challenge

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling
finding: Sequential scaling (budget forcing) beats parallel majority voting at the same compute; REBASE tree search adds more but costs an extra reward-model pass.
numbers: Budget forcing lifts AIME24 from 50% to 57%. In their parallel experiment REBASE scales better than majority voting and even than sequential scaling; majority voting on the base model cannot catch up with sequential scaling. 12 of 30 questions exceeded the context window at 512 steps.
limits: Fine-tuned 32B model on 1K traces; flattening and context limits.
agent_relevance: Longer single-chain thinking is a strong rival to trees; test it before building S6.

source: Koh et al. (2024) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Best-first tree search in a real web environment raises success of GPT-4o agents.
numbers: VisualWebArena GPT-4o+SoM 18.9% to 26.4% (+39.7% relative); WebArena 15.0% to 19.2% (+28.0%); Llama-3-70B VWA 7.6% to 16.7%, WebArena 7.6% to 10.1%. Success scales with test-time compute.
limits: Absolute rates still low; needs a model value function and environment backtracking.
agent_relevance: Search helps most where a real environment gives feedback; still small absolute gains.

source: Besta et al. (2024) Demystifying Chains, Trees, and Graphs of Thoughts
finding: Survey/taxonomy of reasoning topologies. Notes that schemes remain limited to simple tasks like Game of 24 and have high inference costs.
numbers: Qualitative; no new experiments.
limits: Survey claims rest on the original papers, which are mostly author-run. Only abstract and introduction read.
agent_relevance: Evidence for tree prompting is concentrated on a few toy tasks; treat claims as single-source (S).

source: Cross-paper synthesis: ToT Game of 24 across implementations
finding: Game of 24 numbers for ToT differ by model and implementation: 74% (GPT-4, b=5), 19% (GPT-3.5, ToT paper), 20% (GPT-3.5, as ToT baseline in LATS), 100% with LLM-written code search.
limits: Different models and sample counts; no independent exact replication of the 74% was opened.
agent_relevance: The 74% is model-dependent; plan for much less on weak models.

source: Cross-paper synthesis: when search beats voting
finding: Across Snell, Wu, Chen, s1: search gains need a reliable value signal, hold on mid-hard items, and cost 10-20x more than re-ranking for little gain with LLM judges.
numbers: Chen: 10-20x slower, negligible gain, discriminator >=90% needed. Snell: easy items degrade with beam search, hard items gain. Wu: 7B+REBASE beats 34B+vote.
limits: Different tasks and verifiers; mixture of trained PRMs and LM judges.
agent_relevance: Use an idea tree only when a code check exists; otherwise sample and select.

source: Cross-paper synthesis: gaps
finding: No opened source tests an idea tree on open-ended ideation with human-rated novelty; creative writing coherence is the only open-ended test, judged by GPT-4 and humans on a self-made task.
numbers: Creative writing: ToT 7.56 vs CoT 6.93 (GPT-4 judge, 1-10).
limits: Gap, not a finding.
agent_relevance: S6 stays [S]/[D]; measure on our own items before trusting it.

source: Katz et al. (2024) Thought of Search: call-count analysis
finding: Analysis of LLM calls per problem: ReAct and ReWOO make L calls; RAP makes LT + bLT calls; LATS makes 2LT + bLT calls (L depth, T iterations, b branching). Authors find none of the methods sound or complete.
numbers: Game of 24: 4573 states in full space; formula-based call counts exceed a single code-written solver by orders of magnitude.
limits: Worst-case formulas, partly estimated by the authors; actual calls vary.
agent_relevance: Budget for any S6 tree should be set by this arithmetic before the run, in code.
